questions.q: After Jesus and His disciples finished the Last Supper, what action did they take before going out to the Mount of Olives? (Matthew 26:30)
options: They sacrificed a young lamb.
They washed their hands in the bronze basin.
They sang a hymn together.
They blew the shofar (trumpet).
questions.explain: Matthew 26:30 reveals a moment of collective worship before the agony of the garden: "And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives."

questions.q: Reflecting on Peter's denial of Jesus, which of the following modern situations is an example of a Christian denying Christ?
options: Attending church every Sunday and joining the choir
Hiding one's Christian identity out of fear of being mocked or losing a job
Reading the Bible quietly at home during personal devotions
Refusing to cheat during an examination
questions.explain: Just as Peter denied Jesus because he was afraid of the authorities and the crowd, a modern Christian denies Christ when they compromise their faith or hide it out of fear of negative earthly consequences.

questions.q: While suffering on the cross during the ninth hour, Jesus cried out "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" (Matthew 27:46). What does this mean?
options: "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit."
"It is finished."
"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
"Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do."
questions.explain: Matthew 27:46 provides the translation for this cry of agony (quoting Psalm 22): "that is, 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'"

questions.q: According to Matthew 27:38, who were crucified alongside Jesus?
options: Two Roman soldiers who had abandoned their posts
Two religious scribes who committed blasphemy
Two robbers, one on the right and one on the left
Barabbas and a zealot leader
questions.explain: Matthew 27:38 records: "Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left," fulfilling the prophecy that He would be numbered with the transgressors.

questions.q: After His resurrection, Jesus commanded His eleven disciples to travel to a specific region to meet Him for the Great Commission. Where did this meeting take place? (Matthew 28:16)
options: At the temple in Jerusalem
By the Jordan River where He was baptized
In the wilderness of Judea
On a mountain in Galilee to which Jesus had directed them
questions.explain: Matthew 28:16 states: "Now the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain to which Jesus had directed them."

questions.q: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus took three disciples further into the garden with Him while He prayed in deep agony. Who were these three? (Matthew 26:37)
options: Peter, Andrew, and Philip
Peter and the two sons of Zebedee (James and John)
Thomas, Matthew, and Judas
Bartholomew, James, and Thaddaeus
questions.explain: Matthew 26:37 tells us: "And taking with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be sorrowful and troubled." The sons of Zebedee are James and John.

questions.q: What deeply symbolic action did Pontius Pilate perform before the crowd to demonstrate that he considered himself innocent of Jesus' blood? (Matthew 27:24)
options: He tore his governor's robe in half.
He took water and washed his hands before the crowd.
He released a white dove into the sky.
He broke a spear over his knee.
questions.explain: Seeing a riot was starting, "Pilate took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, 'I am innocent of this man's blood; see to it yourselves.'"

questions.q: While praying in the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus fell on His face in deep distress. According to Matthew 26:39, what was His prayer to the Father?
options: "My Father, let fire come down and consume my enemies."
"My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will."
"My Father, send legions of angels to deliver me tonight."
"My Father, why have you forsaken me?"
questions.explain: Demonstrating ultimate submission to God's will despite immense suffering, Jesus prayed: "My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will."

questions.q: During the crucifixion of Jesus, a dramatic and eerie supernatural event occurred over the land from the sixth hour until the ninth hour (from noon to 3:00 PM). What was it? (Matthew 27:45)
options: A continuous lightning storm
An eclipse of the moon
Darkness over all the land
A massive swarm of locusts
questions.explain: Matthew 27:45 records: "Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour." This darkness symbolized divine judgment and the mourning of creation.

questions.q: During Jesus' Triumphal Entry, what did the massive crowds do to honor Him as He rode the donkey towards Jerusalem? (Matthew 21:8)
options: They built a wooden chariot for Him.
They threw gold and silver coins on the path.
They spread their cloaks on the road and cut branches from the trees to lay before Him.
They marched ahead of Him with Roman flags.
questions.explain: Matthew 21:8 states: "Most of the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road," as a traditional act of welcoming a victorious king.

questions.q: During His Triumphant Entry (Luke 19:41-44), what emotionally profound action did Jesus take as He approached and saw the city of Jerusalem?
options: He laughed in triumph.
He wept over it, foreseeing its coming destruction.
He ordered His disciples to build a throne there.
He refused to enter and turned back to Galilee.
questions.explain: Luke 19:41 tells us: "And when he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it," because the people did not recognize the time of God's coming to them, leading to their eventual destruction by Rome.

questions.q: When the crowd came to arrest Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane, one of Jesus' disciples drew a sword and cut off the ear of the high priest's servant. How did Jesus react? (Matthew 26:51-52)
options: He encouraged the other disciples to also draw their swords.
He told him to put his sword back into its place, stating that all who take the sword will perish by the sword.
He ran away while the disciple distracted the guards.
He thanked the disciple for defending Him.
questions.explain: Jesus immediately rebuked the violence, saying, "Put your sword back into its place. For all who take the sword will perish by the sword," and proceeded to heal the servant's ear.

questions.q: When Jesus was crucified, what was written on the charge placed over His head? (Matthew 27:37)
options: "This is Jesus, the Carpenter of Nazareth."
"This is the enemy of the Roman Empire."
"This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
"This man claimed to be God."
questions.explain: Matthew 27:37 states: "And over his head they put the charge against him, which read, 'This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.'"

questions.q: After Jesus resurrected, the Roman guards reported the empty tomb to the chief priests. What deceitful plan did the chief priests devise to cover up the resurrection? (Matthew 28:12-13)
options: They gave the soldiers a large sum of money to say the disciples stole His body while they were asleep.
They claimed that Jesus had secretly paid the guards to let Him out.
They told everyone that an earthquake had swallowed the body into the ground.
They said the body was taken away by a pack of wild animals.
questions.explain: The elders "gave a sufficient sum of money to the soldiers and said, 'Tell people, His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep.'"
